clue.text: Place for union resistance, say — is effort spoiled by hostility?

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
e.g. means 'for example', as 'say' does
taken as written
a try is an attempt or effort
food that has spoiled has gone off
iciness is coldness or hostility

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether a wedding is ruined by hostile relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' is marriage, not a trade union; a register office (popularly registry office) is where British civil weddings take place.
explanation.definitionFit: A civil marriage ceremony is conducted at this local government office, making it a venue for a wedding.

clue.text: Is Rev repeatedly disturbed about editor over sacred text?

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words written out twice
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
on can mean 'about', as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A worried vicar fusses with an editor over the wording of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Each copy of IS REV is rearranged separately: one is followed by ED, the other by ON, with 'over' placing the first part above the second in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Revised Version is the late nineteenth-century English revision of the King James Bible, a sacred scripture.

clue.text: Refuse to put front of BMW under cover

indicators.note: something under cover sits inside a shelter, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a garage gives a car cover

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the car maker's name

explanation.surface: An owner declines to put the car away in shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb to decline, but it is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is rubbish or waste matter, the noun sense of refuse (stressed on the first syllable).

clue.text: It pointedly illuminates English cunning in insult

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult
E is the abbreviation for English
arch means slyly knowing or cunning

explanation.surface: Something sharply exposes the craftiness hidden in an English put-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointedly' sounds like sharp wit, but here it means the beam is aimed at a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A searchlight is a powerful lamp whose beam is directed at a chosen spot, lighting it up.

clue.text: Religious ceremony contributing to spirituality

indicators.note: a part contributing to a whole forms a run of letters inside the next word

parts.note: a run of letters inside this word

explanation.surface: A church service adds to one's spiritual life.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite or formal sequence of acts performed in worship is a ritual.

clue.text: Exaggerates more than some females

parts.note: over means in excess of
does are female deer, rabbits and the like

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone overstates things more than certain women do.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to carry it too far, as one does in exaggerating.

clue.text: Infection reduced and passed quickly, from what we hear

indicators.note: hearing points to the sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: flew is the past tense of fly, to pass quickly

explanation.surface: An illness eased off and was soon over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' belongs to the definition: the word is a shortened form of influenza.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu is the clipped form of influenza, so it is the name of that infection cut down.

clue.text: One in church opposed to Italian red

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
the Roman numeral for one
anti means against

explanation.surface: A lone churchgoer objects to a red-wearing Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in church' reads as containment, but the I simply follows CH, the church abbreviation; 'Italian red' could be a communist, but it is a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Silly female put away her book and showered

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
to put food away is to eat it
taken as written
B is an abbreviation for book
rain showered down

explanation.surface: A scatty woman tidied her book away and took a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone featherbrained is flighty and foolish, as if their head held only feathers.

clue.text: Mostly naive art morphs into another form

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
to morph is to change shape, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the word without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Untutored artwork transforms into something different.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant is a version differing in some respect from the standard, i.e. an alternative form.

clue.text: Slippery European capable of shocking, taking us in

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside

parts.note: a live wire carries current and can give a shock
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shifty continental with a talent for outrage draws Americans in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capable of shocking' suggests scandal, but it is electrical: a live wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elusive is hard to catch or pin down, like a slippery customer.

clue.text: Where people go for spring or start of summer each year

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that one counts

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
p.a. stands for per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers choosing a destination in springtime or at the beginning of summer, year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is a mineral spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a resort built around a mineral spring, visited for the healing waters.

clue.text: French artist upset at clue about evil spirit

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written before the letters are rearranged
a demon is an evil spirit

explanation.surface: A French painter is annoyed by a crossword clue about a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of the water lilies series.

clue.text: Sing amidst mythical sea creatures in ships

indicators.note: amidst means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: mermen are the male counterparts of mermaids
to chant is to sing or intone

explanation.surface: Singing among sirens and the like aboard vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchantmen are trading vessels, i.e. merchant ships, as opposed to warships.

clue.text: Lives finally chronicled by British author

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it modifies

parts.note: the closing letter of this word
H. G. Wells, the English author of The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: Biographies at last written up by a British writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' reads as the plural noun for biographies, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside there, so dwells is a synonym for lives as a verb.

clue.text: It's left here for drivers — and elsewhere, right?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in Britain, where traffic keeps left, the side of a car next to the kerb is the left
second meaning: in countries that drive on the right, the same kerbside is the right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' and 'right' look like 'abandoned' and 'isn't it?', but they are the two sides of a vehicle; the same word names the left side in Britain and the right side abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The nearside of a vehicle is the side nearest the kerb: left in Britain, right in countries that drive on the right.

clue.text: Prepare to serve more that's raw, not initially on menu, for example

indicators.note: not initially means without the opening letter

parts.note: green means raw or inexperienced
a menu is one kind of list

explanation.surface: A cook gets ready to dish up more of something uncooked that's on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' is military service, not dishing up food.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enlist is to sign up again for a further term of military service.

clue.text: Noble leaves much to be desired?

definitions.text: Noble leaves much to be desired?

parts.words: Noble leaves much to be desired?
parts.note: surface reading: an aristocrat proves disappointing

parts.words: Noble leaves much to be desired?
parts.note: setter's reading: tea leaves named after a nobleman, which many people want to drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun for tea leaves, and 'much to be desired' is meant literally: very popular.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a bergamot-flavoured blend of tea named after the 2nd Earl Grey, a British prime minister.

clue.text: Kind of music newspaper issue sent up

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

indicators.note: in a down answer, sent up means written from bottom to top

parts.note: to emit is to issue or send out

explanation.surface: A type of music satirised in a newspaper edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as an edition of the paper, but it is the verb to give out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated style of piano music popular in America around 1900.

clue.text: Sweet child confined within creche? Rubbish

indicators.note: something confined within is enclosed by surrounding letters

parts.note: a run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a sweet child cooped up in a nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic winged child in art, so the word is used of an adorable, innocent little one.

clue.text: Talk informally over wine, producing affinity

parts.note: to rap is to chat in a relaxed way
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Chatting casually over a glass of wine builds a bond.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious relationship of mutual understanding, i.e. a natural affinity.

clue.text: Wrongly blamed for mayhem

indicators.note: something done wrongly is set out incorrectly, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written before the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unjustly held responsible for chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London asylum Bethlem, means uproar and confusion, a synonym for mayhem.

clue.text: The Guinness drunk without prior inspection

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pint of the black stuff downed without anyone checking it first.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness is the famous Irish stout.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying something sight unseen means acquiring it without having looked at it beforehand.

clue.text: Pulse from athlete's first taken after workout

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: An athlete's heart rate is taken after training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but it is the edible seed; 'taken after' puts the letter behind the workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, and the pea is one of them.

clue.text: From old capital I'm returning Japanese art

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old capital' suggests a former capital such as Kyoto; 'old' is a separate abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Trouble and woe, in regular instalments

indicators.note: instalments at regular intervals means taking every other letter

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Hardship and misery arriving bit by bit, like hire purchase payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, as in 'without further ado', so it is a mild synonym for trouble.

clue.text: Ridicule a person in seat — fool around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the others

parts.note: a loon is a crazy or foolish person
taken as written
a Member of Parliament holds a seat in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Mocking someone in a chair as a buffoon fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' is a parliamentary seat, so the person in it is an MP, a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to ridicule them publicly through satire.

clue.text: Reconstructed mine, and acted to clear of pollution

definitions.note: read as an adjective: free of contamination

indicators.note: something reconstructed is rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written before the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebuilt mine where action was taken to clean up the pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like part of 'acted to clear', but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decontaminated has had harmful substances removed, so it is now free of pollution.
